summary: The article describes how small businesses in U.S. cities such as Columbus, Charleston, Lansing, Austin and Denver have adapted since fall 2023 to changing consumer behavior. Owners responded to the shift online, sustainability expectations, supply chain disruptions and the demand for personal connection by adopting technology, going green and sourcing locally. Costs remain a major hurdle, eased somewhat by grants, crowdfunding and community programs.
one_line: Small business owners across the U.S. adapt to post-September 2023 shifts toward online shopping, sustainability, local sourcing and technology despite cost pressures.
key_facts: Since September 2023, a surge in online consumer activity has persisted, pushing small businesses to improve their digital presence.
Jack Reynolds, owner of 'Bean There' café in Columbus, Ohio, saw in-café patronage decline steeply while online orders for his artisanal coffee blends doubled.
Tamara Johnson of 'Bloom Boutique' in Charleston, South Carolina, launched a virtual fitting room in October where customers upload a photo to see how clothes look on them.
On November 10, 2023, 'Cycle Style,' a bike shop in New Hampshire, switched to biodegradable packaging; owner Miguel Santos says being seen as 'green' is 'a real differentiator.'
Starting in December 2023, Emily Chen of 'Blossom Bookstore' in Lansing, Michigan, began hosting author Q&As and book club gatherings via Zoom.
Carlos Gomez, a restaurateur in Austin, Texas, faced suppliers canceling orders with little notice during the late-2023 supply chain slowdown.
By mid-September, Gomez redesigned his menu around locally sourced ingredients, which sped up his supply chain and built local business relationships.
Diana Murphy of Denver launched an app for her gift shop 'Curio Curations' with an AR tool to view products at home and AI that suggests gifts based on a recipient's social media likes and interests.

Laura Hernandez, founder of 'TechTeach', began offering workshops in late September on topics from social media marketing to data analysis to address a digital literacy gap among small business owners.
Investments in technology, training and sustainable practices carry hefty price tags, creating financial pressure while businesses await returns.
Local government grants, crowdfunding and community support programs started in the latter months of 2023 have helped small businesses stay afloat.
Retail outlets have introduced augmented reality, and point-of-sale financing options let smaller businesses compete with larger retailers.
